newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close limit up, hogs up sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close limit up, hogs up sharply.

text.p: CME pork belly futures remained locked up the daily limit of 3.000 cent per lb in all months at the close following Friday's bullish Cold Storage report. Hog futures followed on spillover from bellies and stronger fundamentals to also set some new highs, traders said.
Pork bellies finished limit up with March at 77.325 cents. Hog futures ended up 1.700 to 0.475 cents with April up most at 74.650 cents. July and August set new contract highs.
Pork bellies shot up for limit gains early and remained there for the remainder of the day following Friday's report which showed frozen belly stocks under earlier expectations.

"That (pork belly) figure we got Friday has served as a catalyst to turn the pork complex toward the stronger side," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp. "The storage figures that we had on bellies was the lowest figure for that date since 1987."
The USDA reported that as of February 1 frozen belly stocks totaled 38.041 million lbs, below estimates of 39.7 to 43.2 million lbs.
Levitt added that traders remember how fresh bellies led the wholesale pork complex up last year and they believe the same can happen again.
In belly options, March settled synthetically 1.500 cent higher in March and beyond which pointed to a fairly sharp gain at the start Tuesday.
However, some traders look for resistance to develop as futures prices approach 80.000 cents. The high price may cut off demand for product, they said.

Technicals and expectations of firmer cash markets added to spillover demand from bellies to lift hog futures. April gaped through a trend line at the opening and touched off a string of buy stops that took that month up the daily limit at one point, traders said.

Fundamental strength was also evident in hogs and reflected expectations that packers will pay higher prices for cash hogs again Tuesday. Pork product prices are low compared to beef and demand should increase, they said.
"Some of the pork cuts look attractive to the retail meat buyers right now. The expectation is that we will put $2 or $3 (per cwt) on the hog market this week," Levitt said.

Rand Financials and Refco notably bought hog futures up into buy stops. In hog options, there was call spreading in April, buying 74 calls and selling 77 calls on a one for two basis. There was interest in buying June and July lower strike puts later, pit sources said.
